selection.name: C05 — Codex native workers
selection.role: Native coordinator for bounded delegation, worker messaging, interruption, failure reporting and review. Ownership boundaries remain instructions rather than enforced filesystem isolation.
selection.install_source: Upstream README; evaluated stable rust-v0.160.0, released 2026-10-01.

basis.shows: Explicit guidance for concrete bounded tasks, disjoint write sets, changed-file reporting and review before integration.
Errored and missing workers are reported as failed, with their statuses retained.
Public worker tests distinguish mailbox activity from successful task completion.
Recent stable release explicitly fixes propagation of subagent environment configuration and preparation failures; publishes Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 assets.
Documented Linux installation and platform binaries. Default-branch commit is 2026-10-02; repository is unarchived.
Captured default-branch Linux x86_64 Bazel test succeeded.
Captured Linux clippy check failed; overall default-branch CI was FAILURE, despite target-platform test passes.

selection.name: C10 — Worktrunk
selection.role: Complementary ownership layer: separate branches and worktrees, agent handoffs, review visibility and configurable checks before merging.
selection.install_command: cargo install worktrunk && wt config shell install
selection.install_source: Upstream README; evaluated release v0.80.0 and default-branch commit 85e685e313f7fbc0612c0e055e655c3917e39f29.

basis.shows: Documented installation, isolated worktrees, agent launching, pre-merge hooks and PR/local merge workflows. Commit is 2026-10-01.
Supported parallel-worker pattern: parent creates worktrees and supplies each child its owned path. This is guidance, not enforced write confinement.
2026-09-27 release preserves branches after failed squash commits and protects dirty submodules and remaining worktree files. Includes Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 binaries.
Captured Linux tests succeeded; default-branch check rollup was SUCCESS.

selection.name: C02 — Codex for Claude companion
selection.role: Claude Code entry point for bounded Codex jobs, explicit read-only reviews, returned results and cancellation. Use separate worktrees and require completed review before integration.
selection.install_source: Upstream README at db52e28f4d9ded852ab3942cea316258ae4ef346; release v1.0.6.

basis.shows: Direct Claude Code integration for rescue, review, status, results and cancellation; documented installation requires Node.js ≥18.18 and local Codex.
Task handling preserves actual status and returns raw output, touched files and persistent Codex thread IDs.
Public fixture tests cover authentication failures, retained cancellation records/logs and interruption of running app-server turns.
Latest merged change had successful Ubuntu test/build CI on its pre-merge commit; this is not an exact default-HEAD check.
Release and default-branch commit are 2026-07-08, approximately 86 days old on 2026-10-02: current under the frozen rule, though less recently maintained than other finalists.
Optional Stop gate fails open when Codex is unavailable. It is not a Git integration gate.
Session cleanup removes plugin job artifacts; underlying persistent Codex threads are separate. The plugin does not establish independent edit isolation.

layers.deciding_comparison: The selected complementary set has the most direct documented fit for the specified agent sessions, but no matched evidence establishes workflow superiority. On WSL2, compare native single-agent Codex, Codex workers with Worktrunk and the Claude companion, and equivalently configured OpenHands SDK and Deep Agents graphs. Freeze tasks, models, acceptance checks and budgets; include pre-existing owned edits, an intentional nonzero failure, cancellation after partial edits, session restart and a reviewer-rejected integration. Measure accepted integrations, lost or misattributed edits/results, retained original errors, cancellation latency, complete parent-plus-worker usage, elapsed time and operator intervention. Require independent acceptance and completed relevant review before every integration.
evidence_gaps: The packet contains no completed comparison. Upstream unit tests, CI and framework microbenchmarks do not establish comparative end-to-end worker quality.
Native ownership instructions and Worktrunk child-path guidance are not enforced write confinement. Codex root --worktree does not establish a separate worktree for every native child.

The companion's optional Stop gate is not a mandatory merge gate. Plugin job artifacts are cleaned up and retention is capped; preservation of underlying Codex threads must not be confused with preservation of every plugin artifact.

Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 support is evidenced for Codex and Worktrunk; WSL2 end-to-end behavior and companion macOS arm64 execution were not measured. This coordination requirement does not need the RTX 4090.

All 12 repositories were unarchived, had default-branch commits within 90 days, recent published releases and issue updates around October 1–2. Issue updates do not establish maintainer responsiveness. Some monorepo latest releases concern CLI or language-specific packages.

CI observations are captured check contexts, not exhaustive pass reports. Codex, Beads, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Canvas had failed captured checks; those failures were retained in the judgment.

Source inspection confirmed that OpenHands SDK has native Claude Code/Codex ACP adapters. Its conformance tests demonstrate protocol compatibility rather than completed coding tasks; the linked SWE-bench evaluation was not independently fetched or used to claim superiority.

The mandated ctx_fetch_and_index call was rejected because it required approval while the session approval policy is never. Authorized GitHub API blobs were instead indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search. External documentation and paper pages were not fetched.
Research used 30 GitHub API calls, one web search and one rejected page-fetch attempt.
sources_read: https://api.github.com/graphql — four batched queries retrieved all candidate READMEs, workflow sources, release and issue activity, check results, and the pinned implementation/test sources cited above.
